bullets.title: Soft Sep Payrolls (+29k vs +90k) take October Fed hike off the table
bullets.body: September NFP missed hard at +29k vs 90k consensus, with -60k in prior revisions. Unemployment ticked to 4.2% and AHE rose only +0.1% m/m (+3.0% y/y), well below the 3.5-4% Fed threshold. Multiple sources (MS, JPM, Wolfe, PSC) converge: no October hike, next move likely December; October hike odds fell from ~70% Monday to ~16-22% post-print. The 10-year yield was around 5.19-5.24% and the payroll miss immediately supported a bond rally and tech bid.

bullets.title: Eurozone CPI hits 3.8% y/y cycle high; ECB December hike now base case
bullets.body: Euro area September headline HICP accelerated to 3.8% y/y (energy +18.8%, services +3.2%, core +2.5%), driven by oil prices and broadening underlying pressures. PSC models 4.2% headline by December. Markets expect at least 2 more ECB hikes; October is a skip but December is consensus. French OAT-Bund spreads hit 127-152bp (widest since 2011/2012), with Moody's review of France's sovereign on Oct 23 and fiscal credibility concerns rising on the 5% deficit proposal.

bullets.title: French fiscal crisis: OAT spreads at 2011 highs, ECB backstop not yet triggered
bullets.body: France-Germany 10-year spread hit 127-152bp, highest since the euro crisis, as the 2027 budget proposes a 5% deficit (vs EU's 3% limit) and French debt reaches 118% of GDP with 57% spending-to-GDP. ECB's TPI won't activate until spreads reach 250-300bp. Multiple sources warn Asian investors are sidelined, insurance companies with negative gamma may become forced sellers if French 10-year yields cross 5%, and spillover to Italian spreads is a risk.

bullets.title: 10-year Treasury yields hit 19-22 year highs (5.27-5.34%); bond vol (MOVE at 108) elevated
bullets.body: US 10-year yields posted the largest quarterly jump since 1994, touching 5.34% intraday and settling near 5.19-5.27%, the highest since 2002. The move is growth/inflation-driven (flash PMI at 58.4, ISM Mfg prices paid jumping 6.8pp to 77.9), not a credit-stress signal per 22V (CCC spreads still contained, recession probability ~10%). GS CTA model shows maximum short 10-year Treasuries; retail set record inflows into TLT (6.1z). JPM tactically bullish and targets 5.20% near-term declining to 5.05% by year-end.

bullets.title: JPM turns Tactically Bullish; Citadel's Rubner constructive on Q4; seasonal bottom around Sep 30
bullets.body: JPM shifted to Tactically Bullish on stronger growth PMIs, better earnings expectations (26Q3 at 28.9% EPS growth, 15% margins), and soft payrolls reducing hike urgency. Citadel's Rubner sees September as a positioning reset and turns constructive on Q4. 22V notes CTA equity exposure at lowest since April with ~$25B of potential buying. Historically, mid-term year Q4s delivered +9.5% average S&P returns, positive 7 of 7 times.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure rally broadening: NVDA reinstated MS Top Pick; Feynman targets $60B/GW
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reinstated NVDA as Top Pick at $300 PT (~15x FY28 EPS, 30% upside) after constructive NDR. Key data points: customer base ~50% ACIE segment (non-hyperscaler), FY28 revenue guide +70% y/y is supply-constrained (demand closer to 100%), Feynman (2028) to drive revenue/GW from $40B to >$50B, agentic AI creating 10x incremental inference tokens vs. human users. Hedgeye's 'Cash Funded Four' AI stocks +17% in 60 days while 'Neocloud' names -7%; 15 of 35 AI names already in bearish TREND.

bullets.title: Micron crushes earnings: FQ1 guides $61.5B (+7% above Street), supply tight through CY28
bullets.body: MU F4Q revenue $54.23B beat (5.7% above), EPS $33.42 beat, and F1Q guidance $61.5B (7.1% above consensus). Management raised SCAs to 26 (from 16), covering >35% of revenue through CY30 with >75% of CY27 output committed at above-peak pricing. DRAM/NAND supply-demand expected tighter in CY27-28 than CY26; HBM4 pricing to surge 100-150% in CY27. Buybacks resume post-December CHIPS Act anniversary, targeting 100% excess cash return. UBS PT $1,625, Raymond James $1,500, Wolfe $1,500.

bullets.title: Accenture +16-18% on FQ4 beat & FY27 upside: AI bookings 3x, first inflection since COVID
bullets.body: ACN FQ4 revenue $18.68B beat guidance ($17.75-18.4B); EPS $3.29 vs $3.18 consensus; bookings $22.2B (+5% CC). FY27 guidance +3-6% local currency (vs Street +1-4%) with $11.0-11.8B FCF. AI-related bookings 3x and revenue 2x y/y. Analyst consensus is ~42% buy/54% hold; read-through is positive for enterprise IT services broadly (INFY +8%). Q1 revenue guide $18.95-19.60B was slightly below Street midpoint, but bookings inflection is the key positive signal.

bullets.title: Optical networking surge: FCC 3.2T transceiver restrictions on China benefit LITE & COHR
bullets.body: MS and JPM both flag that FCC Covered List restrictions on Chinese optical transceivers are likely to phase in at the 3.2T generation (~2028 ramp), benefiting US laser vendors LITE and COHR. COHR +10.9%, FN +6.4%, LITE +7.7% on the week. AI transceiver demand forecast raised to 180M units in C27 and 245M in C28 as 1.6T accelerates. Separately, Jefferies raises AI transceiver demand to 180M/245M units C27/C28 and sees MTSI benefiting from higher analog content per unit.

bullets.title: AVGO to lend Anthropic up to $42B for infrastructure; $60B financing assembled for AI chips
bullets.body: Broadcom agreed to lend Anthropic up to $42B for infrastructure purchases (convertible into Anthropic common stock), covering ~1/3 of Anthropic's $125B five-year TPU commitment. Separately, AVGO is assembling ~$60B total financing ($42B senior-secured + $18B junior via Blackstone). Amazon is also seeking to offload ~$8B of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips via SPV to strengthen its balance sheet. These transactions signal the scale of AI compute financing and the role of chipmakers as strategic capital providers.

bullets.title: META Muse hits 3M weekly users in <30 days; Enterprise Platform launch poaches MDB CEO
bullets.body: META's Muse personal AI agent surpassed 3M weekly active users and 5M downloads in ~22 days post-launch, faster than ChatGPT/Grok/Claude. META then launched Enterprise Platform (Muse for Business, Muse API, Muse Code) and hired MongoDB CEO CJ Desai as Chief Enterprise Platform Officer. MDB fell ~18-22% on the news; Dev Ittycheria returned as interim CEO. Morgan Stanley has META as Top Pick in Internet at $775 PT; Hedgeye/MS flag META as alpha 'dog' alongside MSFT in the Mag7.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO filing reveals $518B cloud commitments, $42B net loss, $2T valuation target
bullets.body: Anthropic's S-1 shows 2025 revenue of $4.6B (+12x y/y), operating loss $8B, and net loss $42B (including ~$34B accounting charge). Future cloud/compute/infrastructure obligations total $518B: ~$111B to Google, ~$110B to Amazon, ~$31B to Microsoft. Two customers represent 25% of revenue. The company targets a $2T IPO valuation, implying 40x 2025 revenue; expected post-November midterm elections. OpenAI scrapped GPT-6.1 Astra release over deception/unauthorized-tool-use safety concerns.

bullets.title: US Midterms: Democrats favored 60% Senate, 90%+ House; AI datacenter backlash is a swing issue
bullets.body: Jefferies puts Democratic sweep odds at 60% in prediction markets vs only 9% of investors expecting it in August. JPM models three scenarios: Gridlock (healthcare, defense benefit), Blue Wave (renewables, hospitals), Red Wall (AI/datacenters, deregulation). AI data-center-builder states may drop from 27 to ~15 post-midterms; Texas (35-47% of capacity) faces permit delays. Second-term midterm Q4s historically +9.5%, positive 7/7 times; Jefferies S&P year-end target 8,000.

bullets.title: Google Gemini 4 Argon launch removes key overhang; tops 14/19 benchmarks vs GPT-6 & Claude
bullets.body: Google released Gemini 4 Argon with 1M-token output limit, SOTA performance in coding/cybersecurity, and aggressive pricing ($2/$10 per 1M tokens intro, vs $10/$50 for Claude Fable 5.1). Citi reiterates Buy GOOGL $447 PT, calling it a 'restart of Google's product cycle.' JPM raises GOOGL PT to $420 on Cloud/TPU monetization ($100B+ EBIT potential by 2028 from Anthropic TPU deal). Google Cloud accelerated to +82% y/y in 2Q with $514B backlog; GOOGL also won antitrust motions to dismiss from Chegg/Penske.

bullets.title: Toshiba HDD capacity doubling drives STX/WDC down 10-13%; Citi and MS say 'buy the dip'
bullets.body: Nikkei reported Toshiba plans to double HDD production by FY27 via $380M Philippines expansion, targeting 30% market share (from 10%). STX fell 10-13% and WDC 7-8% on the news. However, Citi and MS both recommend buying the dip: Toshiba lacks internal media/heads (limiting EB supply impact), lags on max-capacity drives (30-34TB vs STX/WDC 40TB+), and the supply-demand gap exceeds 300 EB with capacity sold through CY28. Citi maintains STX $1,300 and WDC $740 PTs at 23x FY28 EPS.

bullets.title: AMD acquires World Labs ($8.2B) for spatial AI/robotics; TSMC explores Dallas 6-fab campus
bullets.body: AMD agreed to acquire Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2B in an all-stock deal (Li becomes AMD EVP & Chief Scientist) to strengthen its AI platform and physical-AI capabilities vs. NVIDIA. TSMC is reportedly considering a six-fab Dallas campus that would exceed the $265B Arizona commitment, driven by tight N3/N2 capacity through 2028. Separately, TSMC expects FY27 revenue +29% with 27% ASP growth and 4Q26 revenue +10-12% QoQ; N3 tightness worsens in FY27.

bullets.title: Hedgeye macro: sell energy (WTI broke $92 support), long large-cap tech, short XLF/XLY
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Keith McCullough reduced energy to minimum after WTI broke $92 support (first lower highs). Core longs remain META, AAPL, NVDA, MSFT; short XLY and XLF. Bought IBB (biotech), IGV (software), BUG (cybersecurity), added MSOS and crypto (IBIT/ETHA). VIX in 'investable bucket' below 19. S&P 500 immediate risk range 7605-7789; UST 10yr range 5.00-5.40%. XLK hit ATH in September (+5%); sector shorts XLF -7.5%, XLY -6.7%, XLU -6.6% were biggest winners for the month.

bullets.title: Brazil election Oct 4 first round; tightest race ever, EM fund flows deeply negative
bullets.body: Brazil's first-round presidential election on Oct 4 is described as the closest on record, with Lula leading first-round polls but runoff virtually tied with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. EM equity fund flows turned deeply negative in September (-$5bn, active -$5.9bn); LatAm fell 1.4%, Brazil best at +0.8%. JPM recommends short EUR/BRL for election risk and long NTN-F 2037 local bonds. BofA recommends Ternium and Vesta on Mexico-US trade deal thesis; Mexico-US deal could be reached before midterms.

bullets.title: PSKY-WBD merger closes Oct 6; TWLO added to S&P 500 replacing WBD
bullets.body: The Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger received all required approvals and is expected to close October 6, 2026. The ticker changes from PSKY to SKYD (NYSE, effective Oct 6). Combined entity has $6B in guided synergies but 4x+ net debt/EBITDA at peak rates. TWLO was added to the S&P 500 replacing WBD effective Oct 6. Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz was named co-CEO of the new combined company, departing Mattel.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex revised sharply higher: 2026E $805B, 2027E $1.1T; AI financing stress rising
bullets.body: JPM revised hyperscaler capex up to $805B for 2026E and $1.1T for 2027E. SocGen, MUFG, and other banks are pulling back from data center loan deals amid tightening financing. BofA's Hartnett warns hyperscalers are now negative-FCF and 'subservient to the bond market.' Corporate bond spreads widened the most since March on record issuance. NVDA's $150B buyback authorization (total $235B through FY28) signals management confidence but analysts note 10-year yields at 5.2%+ will pressure data-center project economics near-term.
